explanation: The pole fires on the typographic apostrophe ’ (U+2019) as an attached clitic: it peaks on the ’ token itself when that ’ follows the last letter of the preceding word and adds a contraction or possessive morpheme (’s, ’t, ’re, ’ve, ’ll, ’d, ’m, or a name-internal ’ — it’s 3.55, didn’t 3.85, What’s 4.02, they’re 2.45, dog’s 3.32, children’s 3.07, O’Brien 2.0, 1990’s 2.9; median 2.81 over the 98 ’ in the 20 scan documents, scale 3.97), with a graded fall-off as the ’ stops carrying the clitic: about half when the host word itself ends in s (boss’s 1.70, class’s 1.61), about a quarter when it follows a plural -s (students’ 0.4, teachers’ 0.1, parents’ 0.2) or closes a quotation that an opening ‘ introduced (‘fine’ 1.0–1.25 versus bare fine’ 2.44, same host and distance), and near rest on the straight ASCII apostrophe (it's 0.79, doesn't -0.1) and on any ’ preceded by a space (it ’s -0.16). The reading is retrospective, not a next-token preparation: the peak is the apostrophe itself and the following token makes no difference (dog’ bone = dog’s = 2.78; boss’ car = boss’s = 1.37), zero-ablating the pole moves next-token probability diffusely (KL 3.7e-3, unconcentrated), the Jacobian lens promotes only whitespace, and the negative pole never leaves its 0.17 resting band; one leftover: at a text's very first position, before any context exists, a few capitalized openers also reach 25–55% of scale (Well 2.24, Okay 2.07, So 1.83, That 1.69, It 1.62, My 1.25).
